answer:
Yes, there is evidence that GLP-1 drugs like semaglutide reduce cardiovascular events. GLP-1 receptor agonists significantly reduce major cardiovascular events and mortality in high-risk populations [5]. Semaglutide has shown potential to improve cardiovascular outcomes in type 2 diabetes [1]. A network meta-analysis found that semaglutide and albiglutide reduce MACE more than other GLP-1RAs and SGLT2 inhibitors [1].

Early versions of GLP-1 drugs, even without much weight loss, reduced MACE by around 20% [4]. All forms of semaglutide now have an FDA label stating they may be useful for preventing heart disease [4]. Semaglutide is FDA-approved for managing type 2 diabetes and reducing cardiovascular risk [3]. GLP-1RAs also reduced myocardial infarction, stroke and cardiovascular death in high-risk individuals [5].
